SurveyNCD: Survey-Weighted Analysis of Self-Reported Health Indicators

Source: R/SurveyNCD-package.R
SurveyNCD.Rd

Analyses population health survey data from the World Health Organization (WHO) Stepwise Approach to Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) Risk Factor Surveillance (STEPS), Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS), Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), and similar complex sample surveys, where chronic conditions are self-reported rather than coded using the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) and estimates must account for stratification, clustering, and sampling weights.

Details

A typical analysis has four steps:

  1. Design: dhs_design(), mics_design(), steps_design() (or any survey/srvyr design).

  2. Clean and score: recode_binary(), multimorbidity_index(), fci_items(), who_anthro_score().

  3. Estimate: survey_prevalence(), mm_prevalence(), mm_standardize() with who_standard_population(), mm_patterns(), mm_bounds().

  4. Inequality: survey_concentration_index(), survey_concentration_curve(), survey_slope_index().

Results can be reported with ncd_table() and plotted with autoplot(). survey_map_indicator(), survey_xgboost(), survey_shap() and plot_shap_summary() are experimental. See vignette("full-workflow") and vignette("real-data-nhanes").

References

Groll, D. L., To, T., Bombardier, C., & Wright, J. G. (2005). The development of a comorbidity index with physical function as the outcome. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 58(6), 595-602. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2004.10.018
